summary: Hand-coded regex detectors for templated text properties (motto, parenthetical, rhetorical question, greeting, sign-off, P.S., emoji, lowercase, etc.) were scored by balanced accuracy against sample labels; a word/bigram scan added majority-pronoun gender. Corpus latent means plus keyword topic labels gave a linear proxy: dependence = g.dF_property / g.dF_topic, cue if |ratio| >= 0.3. The only true-logit texts (8, probe 1) were hand-written fishing/sailing paragraphs with a P.S. or motto appended, used to validate the proxy and confirm P.S. Latents were chosen by a greedy optimizer of predicted dependence removal under a topic-retention band, ranked with minimal-pair deltas. One cue (or none) per probe, 16 latents each.

phases.purpose: Inspect task/corpus files, fetch gradients for all 4 probes and the sample notes
Build property detectors, count phrase inventories in corpus, score balanced accuracy vs sample labels and corpus correlations; refine sign-off detector
Word and bigram scan over sample notes for any further label-perfect property; adds he/she gender
Encode the whole corpus in 6 batches of 64; keyword topic classifier for 8 topics
Gradient x corpus property-split dependence ratio per probe and property; two-topic-restricted variant tried and dropped
8 hand-written probe-1 texts: compare true logits with F@g, measure P.S. and motto insertion effects; fix cues P0 motto, P1 P.S., P2 none, P3 gender
First latent selector (coverage with topic filter); motto coverage found to be low and diffuse
Short minimal pairs for motto and pronoun swap; compare clean vs corpus deltas; sweep topic filters
Greedy removal optimizer; letter-length motto pairs for a realistic motto delta; lock final 16-latent sets
Check regex+scope balanced accuracy vs detector on corpus and vs detector/label on samples
Try raising topic-retention ceiling and topic-suppressor latents for motto (dropped); robustness under two topic estimates

probe_query_use.text_kind: hand-written property-free fishing and sailing paragraphs (2 each), plus one fishing and one sailing paragraph each with a P.S. line appended and with a motto clause appended
probe_query_use.purpose: Validate the F@g linear proxy against true logits and directly measure the P.S. and motto insertion effects relative to topic on probe 1

per_probe.procedure: Motto was label-perfect in samples and had the largest corpus dependence ratio (about -1.76 of the topic effect). Regex = alternation of the six motto phrases counted in the corpus, scope any, checked at balanced accuracy 1.0. Latent selection: greedy maximization of predicted removal with candidates ranked by a delta from letter-length motto minimal pairs and evaluated on the corpus motto split, topic retention kept in [0.9,1.2]. Coverage stayed near a third because the motto signal is spread over hundreds of latents; adding topic-suppressor latents was tried and dropped since none agreed across two topic estimates.

per_probe.conclusion: a P.S. line at the end of the note
per_probe.procedure: No label-perfect property passed 0.3 on the corpus ratio, but P.S. read +0.37 on this probe only (near zero on probe 2). Eight true-logit texts on hand-written fishing/sailing paragraphs showed F@g tracks real logits (corr 0.999) and appending a P.S. moved logits toward fishing by about 3 points while a motto did almost nothing. Ratio taken from the corpus estimate (0.37) since the crafted texts had an inflated topic gap. Regex ^p.s. on last_line. Latents: greedy on corpus P.S. split, retention band [0.9,1.2].
per_probe.quote: Key: `ps` is elevated *specifically* for Probe 1 (+0.373) vs near-zero for the clean none-probe P2 (−0.062), so it's likely a genuine Probe-1 dependence, not a universal artifact.

per_probe.procedure: Every property's corpus dependence ratio was below 0.07 in magnitude against a large topic effect, so the probe was answered none with no further checks or true-logit texts.

per_probe.conclusion: gender of the subject (she/her vs he/him)
per_probe.procedure: Pronoun words surfaced in a word scan as near label-perfect; majority-pronoun gender was label-perfect in all probes and had ratio +1.03 on this probe. Regex \b(she|her)\b, scope any, balanced accuracy 1.0 vs the majority-pronoun detector. Latents: greedy ranked by a delta from two hand-written he/she pronoun-swap pairs (chess and cooking), evaluated on the corpus gender split, retention band [0.85,1.2].
per_probe.quote: Gender (he/she) shows up as near-perfectly confounded — I almost missed it!

caveats: Letter-length motto templates: only two of the eight are reproduced verbatim in the script. Some exploratory sweeps (topic-filter thresholds, retention ceilings) are reconstructed in simplified form. The 0.3 cue threshold is applied to the corpus ratio; the P.S. cue was kept despite failing the exact-label-confound screen, a judgment encoded as a comment. The session stated it would test motto ablation on sample notes but never ran it.
